With the rapid development of digital technologies, many everyday services are transitioning from traditional manual processes to online systems. Web-based applications have become essential tools for improving efficiency, convenience, and accessibility in various sectors including education, commerce, and service industries.

Food courts in universities often experience heavy congestion during peak hours such as lunch breaks. Students usually spend considerable time standing in queues to place orders and collect food. This results in wasted time, overcrowding, and inefficiency for both students and food stall vendors.

has been proposed. CampusBite is a web-based food pre-ordering system designed specifically for college campuses. The system allows students to browse food stalls, view menus, and place orders online before arriving at the stall.

After an order is placed and payment is completed, the system generates a unique order token. This token enables students to collect their food directly from the vendor without waiting in long queues.

Digital ordering systems have become increasingly popular in recent years due to the growth of online commerce and mobile technologies. Many restaurants and food delivery services use online platforms to allow customers to place orders remotely.

Research in service management shows that digital ordering platforms can significantly reduce waiting time and improve operational efficiency. These systems automate order processing, improve communication between customers and vendors, and help businesses manage demand more effectively.

Several studies have also explored queue management techniques in service environments. Long queues are often caused by inefficient ordering processes and limited-service capacity. Implementing online ordering systems allows customers to place orders remotely, thereby reducing congestion at service points.

Role-based web applications have also been widely adopted in modern information systems. These systems assign different permissions to different types of users, ensuring that each user can only access relevant functionalities.

Despite the availability of online ordering systems, most existing platforms are designed for large commercial restaurants rather than campus food courts. Therefore, there is a need for a specialized system that addresses the unique needs of university environments

Students in university food courts frequently experience long waiting times due to manual ordering processes. During peak hours, the large number of students ordering food simultaneously leads to overcrowding and inefficient service.
The lack of a digital ordering system prevents students from placing orders in advance, resulting in unnecessary delays.
The CampusBite platform focuses on providing a digital solution for campus food courts. The system enables:
Menu and stall management for vendors
The system is intended to operate within university campuses and can be expanded to other institutional environments
The primary objectives of the CampusBite system are:
To develop a web-based food ordering platform for university campuses.
To reduce waiting time in food courts by enabling pre-ordering.
To allow vendors to manage food stalls and menu items efficiently.
To generate unique tokens for order identification and pickup.
To provide role-based access control for administrators, vendors, and users.
To improve order management and service efficiency within campus food courts

The CampusBite system provides an efficient solution for managing food ordering within university campuses. By enabling students to pre-order food online, the system reduces waiting times and improves the overall dining experience.

The platform also helps vendors manage orders more effectively and maintain better control over their menu offerings. Through its role-based design and web-based interface, the system ensures accessibility and scalability.
